title: Plural 3: Masculine Genitive (-ов / -ев / -ей)
titleRussian: Множественное число 3: Родительный падеж мужского рода
description: The masculine genitive plural splits three ways. Hard consonants take -ов, soft -й takes -ев, and soft -ь plus ж, ш, ч, щ all take -ей. Triggered by numbers 5+, by нет, много, мало, несколько, and by genitive prepositions.
descriptionRussian: Родительный падеж множественного числа мужского рода имеет три окончания. Твёрдые согласные получают -ов, мягкое -й — -ев, а мягкое -ь и шипящие ж, ш, ч, щ — -ей. Используется после чисел от пяти, после нет, много, мало, несколько и предлогов с родительным падежом.
intro: Here is the case that gives the Russian plural its reputation. The masculine genitive splits three ways, and which ending you get depends on the last letter of the stem rather than on anything meaningful. Worse, one group looks hard and behaves soft. Five very common triggers pull this case, so you will be practicing it constantly whether you want to or not.
rules: Hard masculine consonants take -ов in the genitive plural: журнал → журналов, стол → столов, дом → домов, телефон → телефонов.
Soft masculine -й takes -ев: музей → музеев, трамвай → трамваев. A stress-final -й stem picks up -ёв: бой → боёв.
Soft masculine -ь takes -ей: словарь → словарей, учитель → учителей, медведь → медведей.
The consonants ж, ш, ч, щ take -ей (NOT -ов, even though they look like hard consonants): карандаш → карандашей, нож → ножей, врач → врачей, ключ → ключей.

Five common triggers for the genitive plural: numbers 5+ (пять журналов), много / мало / несколько (много друзей), нет (нет журналов), the prepositions без / у / для / из / от (без ключей), partitive use (хочется чая).

Family-plural masculines split two ways in the gen pl. -ьев for брат → братьев and стул → стульев. -ей for друг → друзей and сын → сыновей. Memorise each as a fixed pair: the pl nom (-ья ending) is shared, but the gen pl ending is not.
examples: В офисе пять журналов. (There are five magazines in the office.) журнал → журналов, hard consonant + -ов.
У Антона много карандашей. (Anton has many pencils.) карандаш → карандашей, ш + -ей.
В библиотеке десять словарей. (There are ten dictionaries in the library.) словарь → словарей, soft -ь + -ей.
В городе много музеев. (There are many museums in the city.) музей → музеев, soft -й + -ев.
Лена часто встречает своих друзей. (Lena often meets her friends.) друг → друзей, the -ья family irregular.
У Ольги нет ключей. (Olga doesn't have her keys.) ключ → ключей, ч + -ей.

items.hint: Recap from L2: animate plural acc borrows which form?
items.explanation: L2 recap: animate plural acc = gen pl. Друг is animate, and its gen pl is the irregular друзей. Today's lesson gives the masculine gen pl its full derivation; the family-plural irregulars (брат → братьев, друг → друзей, сын → сыновей, стул → стульев) join the regular -ов / -ев / -ей patterns.

items.promptEnglish: There are five magazines in the office.
items.hint: After numbers 5+, the noun goes into the genitive plural. Hard masc cons + ?
items.explanation: After numbers 5 and above, the counted noun takes the genitive plural. Hard masculine consonants take -ов: журнал → журналов. Compare numbers 2-4, which call for the genitive singular instead (два журнала).

items.hint: Карандаш ends in ш. The consonants ж, ш, ч, щ take -ей, NOT -ов.
items.explanation: After много + countable plural, the noun takes the genitive plural. The consonants ж, ш, ч, щ take -ей: карандаш → карандашей. The 7-letter rule blocks -ов here even though ш is a hard-looking consonant in the dictionary form.

items.promptEnglish: There are ten dictionaries in the library.
items.hint: Словарь ends in soft -ь. Soft -ь takes which gen pl ending?
items.explanation: Soft -ь masculines take -ей in the gen pl: словарь → словарей. The same -ей ending also covers the consonants ж, ш, ч, щ (карандаш → карандашей, врач → врачей), which is why -ей is the most common ending in the masculine gen pl after -ов.

items.promptEnglish: There are many museums in the city.
items.hint: Музей ends in soft -й. The gen pl ending for soft -й is the third option in our three-way split.
items.explanation: Soft -й masculines take -ев in the gen pl: музей → музеев, трамвай → трамваев. This is the smallest of the three groups; you will meet it less often than -ов or -ей, but it's regular and predictable.

items.promptEnglish: There are seven houses on the street.
items.hint: Дом is hard masc cons. After numbers 5+, the noun goes into the gen pl. Hard cons + ?
items.explanation: Hard masculine consonants take -ов: дом → домов. The L1 irregular pl nom дома (stress-shifted -а) does not affect the gen pl, which keeps the regular -ов ending.

blanks: В магазине много _____. (There are many phones in the shop.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: After много + a countable plural, the noun takes the genitive plural. Телефон ends in a hard consonant, so the ending is -ов: телефонов.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are no keys on the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: Ключ ends in ч, and ж, ш, ч, щ take -ей in the genitive plural, not -ов, even though they look like hard consonants: ключей. Ключов is the trap of applying the default masculine -ов to a husher stem. Ключа is the genitive singular.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There were five brothers in the family.
errorCorrection.explanation: Брат belongs to the -ья family: its plural is built on the soft stem братья, and the genitive plural is братьев. Братов is the trap of applying the hard -ов to a noun that has gone soft in the plural; it is not a real form. The -ья family carries this soft stem through every plural case: братьев, братьям, братьями, братьях.

Сын is in the -ья family (сыновья), but like друг it takes the irregular -ей in the genitive plural: сыновей, not the -ьев of братьев. Сыновьев overgeneralizes the братьев pattern; the -ья family splits between -ьев and -ей and each word must be learned.

minimalPairs.explanation: After много + a countable plural, the noun takes the genitive plural, not the genitive singular. Друга is the singular genitive ('of one friend'); друзей is the plural genitive ('of many friends'). The plural fits after много друзей.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There are five shops in the city.
minimalPairs.explanation: After numbers 5 and above, the counted noun goes into the genitive plural: пять магазинов. Магазины would be the nominative plural ('the shops' as a subject), which doesn't fit after a number 5+.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each masculine noun by its genitive plural ending.

reviewVocab.definition: the genitive plural; the case form used after numbers 5+, after много / мало / несколько / нет, and after the genitive prepositions без / у / для / из / от.
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'У Маши пять журналов' слово 'журналов' стоит в родительном падеже множественного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: the consonants ж, ш, ч, щ; in the masculine gen pl they take -ей (not -ов), behaving like soft consonants even though they look hard.
reviewVocab.example: Карандаш → карандашей, нож → ножей, врач → врачей, ключ → ключей.

reviewVocab.definition: the family-plural masculines (брат, друг, сын, стул); their pl nom takes -ья (братья, друзья, сыновья, стулья). Their gen pl splits two ways: -ьев for брат → братьев and стул → стульев; -ей for друг → друзей and сын → сыновей.
reviewVocab.example: У Маши много братьев и друзей. (Masha has many brothers and friends.)
